title: TE Edward A. Steele III v. Great Lakes Presbytery
disposition_detail: The Committee on Judicial Business found the appeal abandoned because no one was present to represent it. It made no merits ruling on the six specifications of error and did not grant the requested investigation, rescission, or erasure.
first_summary: TE Edward A. Steele III appealed Great Lakes Presbytery's December 7, 1985 action divesting him without censure and without judicial process. He alleged misinterpretation of BCO 34-10, discriminatory treatment, and pastoral injury, and asked the 14th General Assembly to investigate and direct rescission or erasure of his name. No one appeared to represent the appeal, so the Committee on Judicial Business found it abandoned and did not reach the merits.
summary: An appeal challenged Great Lakes Presbytery's decision to divest TE Edward A. Steele III without censure and without judicial process, which he alleged followed an accusation that he was not engaged in his official duties. Steele alleged constitutional and discriminatory error and sought investigation, rescission, or erasure of his name. Because no one appeared to represent the appeal, the Committee on Judicial Business judged it abandoned, leaving the merits and requested relief undecided.
